text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement adjusted by clinical assessment at every visit (weight, blood pressure lying and standing, energy, salt craving, and signs of over- or under-replacement), with sodium, potassium and plasma renin to guide fludrocortisone; doses set with endocrinology
  • Endocrinology consultation to confirm the cause, set the replacement doses, review the thyroid results and bone health, and plan stress dosing and follow-up
  • Written sick-day rules (double the hydrocortisone for fever above 38 °C, triple it above 39 °C, and inject and seek emergency care if vomiting or unable to take tablets), an emergency hydrocortisone injection kit with training, a steroid emergency card and a medical ID, reviewed at every visit
  • Screening for associated autoimmune disease: 21-hydroxylase antibodies for the cause, TSH, free T4 and thyroid peroxidase antibodies, vitamin B12, A1c and celiac serology with total IgA at intake; TSH at least yearly afterwards, and the others yearly or with symptoms
  • Chronic low back pain: physical therapy with core strengthening, swimming, heat, and gradual weaning from the brace except on long journeys; acetaminophen as needed; no opioids; Oswestry Disability Index at each review; imaging only for red flags
  • Bone health: a bone density scan because of corticosteroid exposure in his teens and twenties, calcium and vitamin D from diet, weight-bearing exercise, and avoiding glucocorticoid over-replacement
  • Influenza: oseltamivir for five days, hydrocortisone doubled under the sick-day rules until a day without fever and then back to the usual dose, fluids with salt, and the emergency injection with a 911 call if he vomits or cannot take tablets
  • Autoimmune hypothyroidism: levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, started only after glucocorticoid replacement was secure; TSH 6 weeks after starting, again at 6 months, then yearly; target TSH 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L

resource.title: John F. Kennedy synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care for a 30-year-old legislator three months after primary adrenal insufficiency was diagnosed during an adrenal crisis abroad, on the Endocrine Society 1938 guideline: confirming the cause with 21-hydroxylase antibodies without stopping treatment, bringing hydrocortisone from a discharge dose down to 15 to 25 mg a day in divided doses and adjusting fludrocortisone by blood pressure lying and standing, sodium, potassium and renin, written sick-day (stress-dose) rules taught and then used in an intercurrent febrile illness, an emergency injection kit and medical ID, screening for associated autoimmune disease (thyroid, vitamin B12, celiac disease, diabetes) with a raised TSH confirmed before treatment and levothyroxine started only once glucocorticoid replacement is secure (CMID hypothyroidism monograph), bone health after earlier corticosteroid exposure, and exercise-based care of chronic low back pain after disc surgery on the ACP guideline, with his privacy about the diagnosis respected.
